mainTopic: Pauses in שופר, the link between the blessings and the blasts, and whether the שליח ציבור covers everyone
overview: The amud begins by finishing רבי יוחנן's ruling that the nine שופר blasts may be heard at nine different times of the day, and a ברייתא supports him. The גמרא challenges him twice with cases where a long pause forces one to start over. It answers that the הלל ruling is his teacher's view, and that his instruction to רבי אבהו followed רבי אבהו's own opinion. Next, a ברייתא teaches that the blasts and blessings of a תענית do not depend on each other, but on ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים they do. רבה explains why: מלכיות, זכרונות and the שופר form one request from הקדוש ברוך הוא. The גמרא learns from the משנה that the blasts should follow the order of the blessings, and רבא and a ברייתא limit this to a חבר עיר. The ברייתא adds that the שופר comes before the blessings, even when the שופר is uncertain and the blessings are certain. Finally, the חכמים and רבן גמליאל argue over whether the שליח ציבור fulfills everyone's obligation, and later sages disagree about whether the חכמים conceded. The גמרא then questions how רבי יוחנן's view was reported.

steps.title: Nine blasts spread over the day still count
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי יוחנן's ruling: hearing the nine blasts at nine different times of the day fulfills the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone heard the nine שופר blasts at nine different times during the day, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the end of רבי יוחנן's ruling. The blasts do not have to come one right after another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The required blasts are nine in total. רבי יוחנן says they can be heard with long gaps between them, even hours apart, and they still add up to a complete מצוה.

phrases.english: the nine blasts at nine different times of the day —
he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּשַׁע תְּקִיעוֹת בְּתֵשַׁע שָׁעוֹת בַּיּוֹם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breaks between the שופר blasts, even long ones, do not ruin the מצוה.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same ruling and adds cases: nine people blowing at once does not count, while hearing different blasts from different people does count, even with breaks and even across the whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this. If someone heard nine blasts at nine times of the day, he fulfilled the מצוה. If he heard them from nine people all blowing at once, he did not. If he heard a תקיעה from one person and a תרועה from another, he fulfilled it, even with breaks between them and even over the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבי יוחנן said. This backs up his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees that gaps are fine. It draws one limit: nine blasts all at the same moment from nine people do not count, because he did not hear nine separate blasts one after another. It also allows mixing blowers, so each blast can come from a different person.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא also teaches this, as support

steps.whatToRemember: Breaks between the blasts are fine, and different people may blow them. Nine blasts at once from nine people do not count.

phrases.english: This is also taught in a ברייתא:
If one heard nine blasts
at nine different times of the day, he has fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.aramaic: מִתִּשְׁעָה בְּנֵי אָדָם כְּאֶחָד — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: If he heard them from nine people at once, he has not fulfilled it.
A תקיעה from this one and a תרועה from that one: he has fulfilled it.
And even with breaks in between,
and even over the entire day.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 1
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that breaks between blasts are acceptable
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the identical ruling plus extra cases

steps.title: Challenge: רבי יוחנן said a long pause means starting over
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן can allow breaks, when he himself said that a long pause during הלל or מגילה means going back to the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: during הלל or the מגילה, if someone paused long enough to have finished the whole thing, he must go back to the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's ruling using another statement he made. The two statements seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For הלל and מגילה, a long pause breaks the reading, and you must start over. For שופר, רבי יוחנן said even hours of gaps are fine. The same person seems to hold two opposite rules about pauses.

keyTerms.meaning: but did he really say...? (opens a challenge)
he goes back to the beginning

phrases.english: And did רבי יוחנן really say this?
But didn't רבי יוחנן say
in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק:
During הלל and the מגילה,

phrases.aramaic: אִם שָׁהָה כְּדֵי לִגְמוֹר אֶת כּוּלָּהּ —
phrases.english: if he paused long enough to finish all of it,
he goes back to the beginning!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling from steps 1 and 2
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that breaks between שופר blasts are fine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן also said a long pause in הלל or מגילה requires starting over, which contradicts allowing breaks in שופר.

steps.title: One ruling is his own, the other is his teacher's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the שופר ruling is רבי יוחנן's own view, while the הלל ruling is his teacher's view, which he only passed on.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not a problem. This one, about שופר, is his own view. That one, about הלל and מגילה, is his teacher's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The two statements come from two different people, so there is no contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלל ruling was said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק. So it shows his teacher's opinion, not necessarily רבי יוחנן's. רבי יוחנן himself holds that a pause does not force you to start over.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is his own view, and that is his teacher's view.
phrases.notes: The teacher is רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, in whose name the הלל ruling was said.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא דִידֵיהּ הָא דְרַבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the statements between two different authorities
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements are רבי יוחנן's personal view, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the שופר ruling is his own view. The הלל ruling belongs to his teacher.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי יוחנן himself told רבי אבהו to start over
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן truly does not hold the 'start over' rule, since he told רבי אבהו to restart קריאת שמע after a long pause in a filthy alley.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't he hold that way himself? But רבי אבהו was once walking behind רבי יוחנן and reading קריאת שמע. When he reached filthy alleys, he stopped. After he passed through, he asked רבי יוחנן: May I finish from where I stopped? He answered: If you paused long enough to finish the whole thing, go back to the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 4. A story shows that רבי יוחנן personally ruled that a long pause means starting over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said the 'start over' rule was only his teacher's view. But here רבי יוחנן gives that same rule in his own ruling to his student, about קריאת שמע. So it seems to be his own view after all, and the contradiction with שופר comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: and doesn't he himself hold this?
may I finish (from where I stopped)?

steps.confusionAlert: The story is about קריאת שמע, not שופר. It is brought only to show what רבי יוחנן himself holds about long pauses.

phrases.english: And is it not his own view?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ הֲוָה שָׁקֵיל וְאָזֵיל
phrases.english: But wasn't רבי אבהו walking along
behind רבי יוחנן
and he was reciting קריאת שמע,
when he reached filthy alleyways, he fell silent,
after he passed through, he said to him:
What about finishing it?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אִם שָׁהִיתָ כְּדֵי לִגְמוֹר אֶת כּוּלָּהּ —
phrases.english: He said to him: If you paused long enough to finish all of it,
go back to the beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִידֵיהּ לָא? וְהָא רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ הֲוָה שָׁקֵיל וְאָזֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the 'start over' rule is only his teacher's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן personally told רבי אבהו to restart קריאת שמע after a long pause, so the rule is his own view too, and it again clashes with his שופר ruling.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was ruling for רבי אבהו's view, not his own
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן told רבי אבהו to restart only because רבי אבהו holds the 'start over' rule; רבי יוחנן himself does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant: 'I myself do not hold this rule. But you do hold it. So for you, if you paused long enough to finish the whole thing, go back to the beginning.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5. רבי יוחנן's instruction to רבי אבהו was based on רבי אבהו's opinion, not his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that רבי יוחנן seemed to hold the 'start over' rule, since he told רבי אבהו to restart קריאת שמע. The answer is that he was only telling רבי אבהו how to act by רבי אבהו's own view. So רבי יוחנן's personal view, that breaks are fine, still stands, and so does his שופר ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: for me, in my own view
I hold, I am of the opinion

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's own view is that a long pause does not force you to start over. That is why nine blasts heard at nine different times still count.

phrases.english: This is what he said to him:
For me, I do not hold this;
but for you, since you do hold it:

phrases.aramaic: אִם שָׁהִיתָ כְּדֵי לִגְמוֹר אֶת כּוּלָּהּ
phrases.english: if you paused long enough to finish all of it
phrases.notes: 'All of it' means the whole קריאת שמע from the story with רבי אבהו.

phrases.english: go back to the beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by reading רבי יוחנן's instruction as addressed to רבי אבהו's opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Personal view versus advice given according to the other person's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's telling רבי אבהו to restart shows that רבי יוחנן holds the 'start over' rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן personally rejects the rule. He only applied it to רבי אבהו, who accepts it.

steps.title: On ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים the blasts and blessings are all required
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: the blasts and the added blessings of a תענית (fast day) do not hold each other back, but the blasts and blessings of ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים do.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The blasts do not hold each other back. The blessings do not hold each other back. But the blasts and blessings of ראש השנה and of יום הכיפורים do hold each other back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It sets up a contrast: usually missing one piece does not ruin the rest, but on ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים every piece is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Holding each other back' means that if one piece is missing, the others do not count either. On a תענית, each blast and each added blessing stands on its own. On ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים they depend on each other. The next steps will ask why.

keyTerms.meaning: hold back; one missing piece stops the others from counting
blessings, here the special blessings added to the תפילה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: תְּקִיעוֹת — אֵין מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ.
phrases.english: The blasts do not hold each other back.
phrases.notes: In other words, if one blast is missing, the other blasts still count.

phrases.aramaic: בְּרָכוֹת — אֵין מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ.
phrases.english: The blessings do not hold each other back.
The blasts and blessings of Rosh HaShanah
and of Yom Kippur do hold each other back.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about whether the pieces of the מצוה depend on each other.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blasts and blessings of a תענית do not hold each other back, but those of ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים do.

steps.title: Why are the Rosh HaShanah pieces all required
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ראש השנה exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why ראש השנה is different, which sets up רבה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a rule without a reason. The גמרא wants to know why the ראש השנה blasts and blessings must all be present when other days' do not.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule taught in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the blasts and blessings of ראש השנה hold each other back.

steps.title: מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות form one package
steps.stepSummary: רבה: הקדוש ברוך הוא asked for מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות together, with the שופר as the means, so they are one unit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: הקדוש ברוך הוא said, 'On ראש השנה say before Me מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות. מלכיות, so that you crown Me King over you. זכרונות, so that your remembrance comes before Me for good. And with what? With the שופר.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question from step 8. The three blessings and the שופר are one request from הקדוש ברוך הוא, so every part is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part has its own job: מלכיות crowns הקדוש ברוך הוא, זכרונות brings us to be remembered for good, and the שופר is how it is all done. Because they work together as one plan, leaving out one piece breaks the whole thing. That is why they 'hold each other back.'
steps.whatToRemember: On ראש השנה the three blessings and the שופר are one unit, so each piece is required.

phrases.english: Rabbah said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Say before Me on Rosh HaShanah
Kingship, Remembrances, and Shofar verses.
Kingship, so that you make Me King over you;
Remembrances, so that there may come before Me
your remembrance for good;
and with what? With the shofar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason requested in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blessings and the שופר are one request from הקדוש ברוך הוא, so each part depends on the others.

steps.title: The משנה's case of a שופר that arrived after the blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: someone who said the blessings and only later got a שופר blows the sets of blasts afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who said the blessings and only afterward got a שופר blows a תקיעה, a תרועה and a תקיעה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from our משנה. It is setting up a close reading in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows the blasts to come after all the blessings when the שופר showed up late. On its own this sounds like the order does not matter. The next step will show what the line quietly implies.

phrases.english: One who said the blessings
and afterward a shofar became available to him
blows a tekiah, a teruah, and a tekiah.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁבֵּירַךְ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְמַנָּה לוֹ שׁוֹפָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a new line of the משנה about the order of blasts and blessings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the שופר became available only after the blessings, he blows the sets of blasts afterward.

steps.title: With a שופר from the start, the blasts follow the order of the blessings
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's permission applies only because there was no שופר at first. With a שופר from the start, the blasts must be heard in the order of the blessings.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he may blow afterward is that he had no שופר at the start. But if he had a שופר at the start, when he hears the blasts he must hear them in the order of the blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely and pulls out a hidden rule: normally the blasts go together with the blessings, one set after each blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's permission depends on a special situation: the שופר came late. So in the normal case, where the שופר is there from the start, the blasts belong in their place among the blessings. This fits רבה's idea that the blessings and the שופר are tied together.

keyTerms.meaning: in the order of the blessings

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not mean the order never matters. Blowing everything after the blessings is allowed only because the שופר arrived late.
steps.whatToRemember: With a שופר on hand from the start, one set of blasts is blown after each special blessing.

phrases.aramaic: טַעְמָא דְּלָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ שׁוֹפָר מֵעִיקָּרָא,
phrases.english: The reason is that he did not have a shofar at the start;
but if he had a shofar at the start,
when he hears them
he hears them in the order of the blessings.
phrases.notes: אַסֵּדֶר is a short form of עַל סֵדֶר, 'according to the order.'

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּלָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ שׁוֹפָר מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a close-reading inference from the משנה line quoted in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Ideally the שופר blasts are heard in the order of the blessings. Blowing them all afterward is allowed only when the שופר was not available at the start.

steps.title: רב פפא בר שמואל asks to hear the שופר after each blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא בר שמואל, praying alone, told his attendant to blow the שופר whenever he signaled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא בר שמואל stood up to pray. He told his attendant: When I signal to you, blow the שופר for me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story of a sage who applied the rule from Step 11 to his own private prayer. This sets up רבא's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said that if a שופר is available, the blasts are heard in the order of the blessings. רב פפא בר שמואל took this to apply to him praying alone, so he wanted blasts after each blessing of מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות.

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל קָם לְצַלּוֹיֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa bar Shmuel stood up to pray,
he said to his attendant:
When I signal to you, blow for me.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל קָם לְצַלּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a sage applying Step 11's rule to an individual praying alone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An individual praying alone had the שופר blown after each blessing.

steps.title: רבא: the order of the blessings matters only in a community setting
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells him the rule of blowing in the order of the blessings applies only in a חבר עיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: They said this only for a חבר עיר (a community praying together).
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on what רב פפא בר שמואל did. The rule about blowing in the order of the blessings is only for a community, not for one person alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11's rule now has a limit. In a חבר עיר the blasts must follow the order of the blessings. A person praying alone does not need this, so the attendant did not have to wait for signals.

keyTerms.meaning: a community gathering praying together (a congregation)
they only said it in the case of

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
They said it only for a community gathering.
phrases.notes: "It" is the rule from Step 11, hearing the blasts in the order of the blessings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: לֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא בְּחֶבֶר עִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא בר שמואל's practice by narrowing Step 11's rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that an individual praying alone must hear the blasts in the order of the blessings.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule was only said for a חבר עיר.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the blasts follow the order of the blessings only in a חבר עיר; elsewhere they only need their own order.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way: When he hears the blasts, he hears them in order and in the order of the blessings. When is this said? In a חבר עיר. But not in a חבר עיר, he hears them in order but not in the order of the blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets out two separate needs. Blasts heard 'in order' (each set done properly) is always required. Hearing them in the 'order of the blessings' is only required in a חבר עיר, just like רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: it is also taught this way (a ברייתא that supports)
in what case was this said?

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different 'orders' here. 'In order' means each set of blasts is blown correctly. 'In the order of the blessings' means blowing after each blessing. Only the second one depends on a חבר עיר.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
When he hears them, he hears them in order,
and in the order of the blessings.
When is this said? In a community gathering.
But not in a community gathering,

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמְעָן עַל הַסֵּדֶר וְשֶׁלֹּא עַל סֵדֶר בְּרָכוֹת.
phrases.english: he hears them in order, but not in the order of the blessings.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's statement with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that the order of the blessings is only needed in a חבר עיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that makes the same distinction.
steps.whatToRemember: The blasts must always be in proper order, but they need to follow the order of the blessings only in a חבר עיר.

steps.title: One person may blow for another but may not say the blessings for him
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a friend can blow the שופר for someone, but cannot say the ברכות of מוסף for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: An individual who did not blow, his friend blows for him. An individual who did not say the blessings, his friend does not say the blessings for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a new rule: someone else can do the blowing for you, but not the blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hearing the שופר from someone else counts as your own מצוה. But when an individual did not say the special מוסף blessings, a friend cannot say them on his behalf.

keyTerms.meaning: an individual (not part of a congregation)
says the blessings on his behalf

phrases.english: And an individual who did not blow,
his friend blows for him,
and an individual who did not say the blessings,
phrases.notes: The "blessings" are the special מוסף blessings: מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות.

phrases.english: his friend does not say the blessings for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיָחִיד שֶׁלֹּא תָּקַע חֲבֵירוֹ תּוֹקֵעַ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא moves on to a new rule about doing the מצוה for someone else.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Another person may blow the שופר for an individual, but may not say the blessings for him.

steps.title: Going to the town with the שופר comes first
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that the שופר comes before the blessings: given two towns, go to the one where they blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה is more with those who blow than with those who say the blessings. How so? Two towns: in one they blow and in the other they say the blessings. One goes to the place where they blow, and does not go to the place where they say the blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a priority rule: if you must choose, choose the שופר over the blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a real case. There are two towns, one with someone who can blow and one with someone who knows the blessings. You go to the שופר town.

phrases.english: And the מצוה is more with those who blow than with those who bless.
How so?
Two towns:
in one they blow, and in the other they say the blessings;
one goes to the place where they blow,
and one does not go to the place where they say the blessings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִצְוָה בְּתוֹקְעִין יוֹתֵר מִן הַמְבָרְכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא continues with a priority rule between the שופר and the blessings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If you must choose, go to the town where they blow the שופר rather than where they say the blessings.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to say this. The שופר is דאורייתא and the blessings are דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious! This one is from the Torah, and that one is rabbinic!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's last rule as too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blowing the שופר is a Torah מצוה. The special מוסף blessings are a rabbinic rule. Of course the Torah מצוה comes first, so why teach it?

phrases.english: It is obvious!
This one is from the Torah, that one is rabbinic!
phrases.notes: "This one" is the שופר, a Torah מצוה; "that one" is the blessings, a rabbinic rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא — הָא דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, הָא דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ברייתא's rule in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that the שופר town comes first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah מצוה obviously comes before a rabbinic one, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The שופר wins even when it is only uncertain
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed for when the blessings are ודאי and the שופר is only a ספק. Even then, go to the שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for the case where this one is certain and that one is only doubtful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is teaching something new. Go to the שופר town even when it is uncertain the שופר will be blown there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a sure rabbinic מצוה beats a מצוה from the Torah that might not happen. The ברייתא teaches that even a ספק of the Torah מצוה outranks a ודאי of the rabbinic one.

keyTerms.meaning: it is only needed for (this case)

steps.whatToRemember: The שופר (דאורייתא) comes before the מוסף blessings (דרבנן), even when the blessings are ודאי and the שופר is only a ספק.

phrases.english: No, it is needed

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּהָא וַדַּאי וְהָא סָפֵק.
phrases.english: for when, even though this one is certain and that one is doubtful.
phrases.notes: The blessings in one town are sure to happen; the שופר in the other town might not happen.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּהָא וַדַּאי וְהָא סָפֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ruling to a new case (לא צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A certain rabbinic מצוה might beat a doubtful Torah מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a doubtful שופר comes before certain blessings.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: every individual is obligated like the prayer leader
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. It says that just as the שליח ציבור must pray, so must every individual. רבן גמליאל disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: Just as the prayer leader is obligated to pray, so too every single person is obligated, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new topic by quoting the משנה. It is setting up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים hold that every person must say the תפילה himself. רבן גמליאל holds that the שליח ציבור fulfills the obligation for the whole group. The next steps explore this argument.

keyTerms.meaning: The prayer leader who prays out loud for the congregation

phrases.english: Just as the prayer leader is obligated,
so too each and every individual, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה, where רבן גמליאל says the prayer leader fulfills the obligation for everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁשְּׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, moving away from the שופר discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every individual is obligated in the ראש השנה prayers, like the שליח ציבור. רבן גמליאל disagrees.

steps.title: The חכמים ask: why does the congregation pray at all?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the חכמים challenging רבן גמליאל. If the leader prays for everyone, why does the congregation say the silent עמידה?
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: The חכמים said to רבן גמליאל: According to you, why does the congregation pray?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רבן גמליאל's view by pointing to the common practice that everyone says the quiet עמידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שליח ציבור's prayer covers everyone, the private prayer of each person seems pointless. The חכמים use the accepted practice to question his view.

phrases.english: It was taught: They said to Rabban Gamliel:
According to your words, why does the congregation pray?
phrases.notes: He means the quiet עמידה that everyone says before the leader repeats it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: לִדְבָרֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבן גמליאל's side of the argument in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's view that the שליח ציבור fulfills the obligation for everyone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the leader covers everyone, the congregation's own silent prayer would be unnecessary, yet everyone says it.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל answers: to give the leader time to prepare
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל explains that the congregation prays quietly so the שליח ציבור can get his prayer ready.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: So that the prayer leader can put his prayer in order.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל answers the challenge. The quiet prayer is mainly there to help the leader prepare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silent עמידה is not proof that each person needs to fulfill his own obligation. Its main purpose is to give the שליח ציבור a chance to organize his prayer before saying it out loud.

keyTerms.meaning: To arrange, to put in order

phrases.english: He said to them: In order to arrange
the prayer leader his prayer.
phrases.notes: Read it as: so that the prayer leader can get his own prayer ready while everyone prays quietly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: כְּדֵי לְהַסְדִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The congregation prays because each person must fulfill his own obligation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The congregation prays so the שליח ציבור can prepare his prayer.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל asks back: why does the leader repeat the prayer?
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל turns the question around. If everyone must pray for himself, why does the שליח ציבור go up and pray out loud?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to them: According to you, why does the prayer leader go down before the ark?
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבן גמליאל challenges the חכמים, using another common practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every person must pray himself and the leader does not cover anyone, the leader's loud repetition seems to have no purpose. Each side's practice now needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes down before the ark, meaning he leads the prayer out loud

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to them: According to your words,

phrases.aramaic: לָמָּה שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר יוֹרֵד לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה?
phrases.english: why does the prayer leader go down before the ark?
phrases.notes: The leader stood in a lower spot in front of the ark, so 'going down' means leading the prayer out loud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: לְדִבְרֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending himself, רבן גמליאל now challenges the חכמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's view that each individual must pray himself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no one is covered by the leader, his loud repetition of the prayer would be pointless.

steps.title: The חכמים answer: for someone who doesn't know how to pray
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the leader repeats the prayer to cover people who cannot pray on their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: To fulfill the obligation of someone who is not an expert.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים defend their view. The leader's repetition is only for those who cannot say the prayer themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים agree that the leader can cover someone. They limit it to a person who is not בקי, meaning he does not know the prayers. Someone who knows how must pray himself.

keyTerms.meaning: To fulfill someone else's obligation for him
An expert, someone who knows the prayers

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: כְּדֵי לְהוֹצִיא אֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּקִי.
phrases.english: They said to him: In order to fulfill the obligation of one who is not an expert.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: כְּדֵי לְהוֹצִיא אֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבן גמליאל's challenge in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the practice to a specific group
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The leader's repetition must mean he covers everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leader covers only those who are not experts.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: if he can cover the non-expert, he can cover the expert too
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל rejects the חכמים's answer. If the leader can fulfill the obligation for one person, there is no reason he can't for another.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Just as he fulfills the obligation of one who is not an expert, so too he fulfills the obligation of the expert.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל pushes back on the חכמים's answer and gets the last word in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the חכמים admit that the leader's prayer can count for someone else, רבן גמליאל argues it should count for everyone. Being an expert should not make the leader's prayer weaker.
steps.whatToRemember: In the ברייתא, each side challenges the other. רבן גמליאל ends with: if the leader can cover the non-expert, he can cover the expert too.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמּוֹצִיא אֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּקִי,
phrases.english: He said to them: Just as he fulfills the obligation of one who is not an expert,
so too he fulfills the obligation of the expert.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמּוֹצִיא אֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּקִי, כָּךְ מוֹצִיא אֶת הַבָּקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the חכמים's answer in step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The חכמים's distinction between the expert and the non-expert.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If the leader's prayer works for one person, nothing makes it fail for an expert.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the חכמים agreed with רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that in the end the חכמים agreed with רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The חכמים agree with רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא tells us how the argument in the ברייתא ended. According to this report, the חכמים gave in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן claims that the argument in the ברייתא did not stay open: in the end the חכמים accepted רבן גמליאל's position. The next steps bring רב, and then ריש לקיש, who say the dispute remains.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority who argued with רבן גמליאל

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The Sages concede to Rabban Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מוֹדִים חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion about how the argument in the ברייתא ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, the חכמים finally accepted רבן גמליאל's view.

steps.title: רב: it is still an argument
steps.stepSummary: רב disagrees and says the חכמים never gave in. The argument is still open.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב said: It is still a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion says the חכמים did not agree with רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב directly disputes רבי יוחנן's claim from step 25. In his view the חכמים never accepted רבן גמליאל's position, so the two sides still disagree.

phrases.english: And Rav said: It is still a dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אֲמַר: עֲדַיִין הִיא מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוחנן's statement in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים never accepted רבן גמליאל's view; the argument is still open.

steps.title: רבי חייא reports רב's view to רב דימי בר חיננא
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא, son of רבה בר נחמני, heard the teaching and repeated it to רב דימי בר חיננא, quoting רב that it is still a dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא, son of רבה בר נחמני, heard this. He went and said the teaching before רב דימי בר חיננא. He told him: This is what רב said: It is still a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about how this teaching was passed along. It is setting up רב דימי's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא brings רב's view, that the argument is still open, to רב דימי. This sets up a surprising point: רב דימי will say that רבה בר בר חנה also reported this view.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him, in front of him

phrases.aramaic: שַׁמְעַהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר נַחְמָנִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya, son of Rabba bar Naḥmani, heard it,
he went and said the teaching
before Rav Dimi bar Ḥinnana.
He said to him: This is what Rav said:
It is still a dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁמְעַהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells how רב's view was passed along.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's view that it is still a dispute was brought to רב דימי בר חיננא.

steps.title: רב דימי: רבה בר בר חנה also reported that ריש לקיש disagreed with רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי says רבה בר בר חנה reported the same view. When רבי יוחנן said the חכמים agreed, ריש לקיש argued and said it was still a dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבה בר בר חנה also said this. When רבי יוחנן said this teaching, ריש לקיש disagreed with him and said: It is still a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי replies that the 'still a dispute' view is not only רב's. רבה בר בר חנה also reported it, as ריש לקיש's response to רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we learn that the full report of רבה בר בר חנה included two sides. רבי יוחנן said the חכמים agreed, and ריש לקיש said they still argued. So רב's view has support from ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: ריש לקיש, the study partner of רבי יוחנן

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה נָמֵי הָכִי קָאָמַר.
phrases.english: He said to him: Rabba bar bar Ḥana also says this.
phrases.notes: רב דימי is speaking here, answering רבי חייא.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא,
phrases.english: When Rabbi Yoḥanan said this teaching,
Reish Lakish disagreed with him
and said: It is still a dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה נָמֵי הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the report in step 27 by adding what רבה בר בר חנה also said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש, like רב, held that the חכמים still disagree with רבן גמליאל.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה בר בר חנה did not say 'still a dispute' as his own view. He was reporting that ריש לקיש said it in response to רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Did רבי יוחנן really say the חכמים agreed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the report about רבי יוחנן. Another student quoted him as saying 'the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל', and that wording implies the argument is still open.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did רבי יוחנן really say this? Didn't רבי חנה of ציפורי say in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל? Saying 'the הלכה' shows that they still disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two reports of רבי יוחנן seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only need to decide 'the הלכה follows X' when people are still arguing. So רבי יוחנן's ruling in רבי חנה's report implies the חכמים never agreed. That contradicts רבה בר בר חנה's report that the חכמים agreed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows an important rule for reading the גמרא: deciding 'the הלכה follows someone' implies the argument is still alive.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yoḥanan say this?
phrases.notes: 'This' means the statement that the חכמים agree with רבן גמליאל.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חָנָה צִיפּוֹרָאָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Ḥana of Tzippori say that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The halakha is like Rabban Gamliel.
Saying 'the halakha' implies that they disagree!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר
